quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Should you drive on the shoulder to pass a car?

options.text: Yes, if the car ahead is turning left.
No, never.
Yes, if the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Never pass another vehicle on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull onto the road.

questions.question: When entering or exiting a driveway, drivers must:

options.text: Have the right-of-way.
Yield to pedestrians.
Honk at pedestrians to move them faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When crossing a sidewalk to enter or exit a driveway, you must yield to pedestrians. Never drive on a sidewalk except to cross it.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
Only check the rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often, to see how traffic is moving behind you.
Only to check your blind spots.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often, to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Frequently check your rearview mirrors while driving so you know where vehicles near you are located.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard.
Keep a steady speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed.
questions.explanation: When being passed, keep your speed steady. Do not speed up or brake. Let the other vehicle merge safely back into your lane.

questions.question: Which statement about medication and driving is true?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make a person drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines cannot affect your driving if taken as directed.
Prescription medicines are always safe to take before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make a person drowsy.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy. You are responsible for knowing how your medication affects your ability to drive.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at the same time.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: Find a gap large enough to safely enter the traffic. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless you cannot find a safe gap to merge into.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign shows a pedestrian crossing. When you see it, be alert and let pedestrians cross the road safely.

questions.question: On a multilane road, what does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: No passing is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from the side of the dashed line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed only from the side of the dashed line.
questions.explanation: When a dashed line is next to a solid line, only traffic on the dashed line side may pass. Traffic on the solid line side may not pass.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered railroad gate. Once the gate is raised, wait until you can see clearly in both directions before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is safe.
Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
Your driving speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous. Drivers behind you may get frustrated and make unsafe moves to pass. Drive with traffic flow and stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
Expect other drivers and pedestrians to see you.
Drive close to the parked cars to give more room to moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your car and parked cars. A person may step out without looking. A driver may start moving their car without seeing you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway starts.
Divided highway ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the divided highway ends ahead. Be ready to change lanes or move your position.

questions.question: When a cyclist is turning left:

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut through all lanes.
They may wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Expect to see cyclists riding with traffic on the road. Do not be surprised if a cyclist uses the left lane to turn.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane:

options.text: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.
You must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to warn them.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians may carry a white cane or use a guide dog. You must yield to them.

questions.question: Where is a U-turn not allowed?

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near curves or hills.
On a straight road where you can see 500 feet ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near curves or hills.
questions.explanation: Never turn around on or near a curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians and may cause a crash.

questions.question: When pulling into traffic from a parked spot, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a gap large enough to match the speed of traffic.
Wait for two vehicles to pass, then drive in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough to match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a gap large enough for your car to reach the speed of other vehicles.

questions.question: When should you not use your horn?

options.text: When you cannot see ahead clearly.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Using your horn near a blind pedestrian can be dangerous. Yield and proceed when safe.

questions.question: If a tire blows out, you should:

options.text: Press the brake hard.
Hold the wheel tightly and brake gently.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the wheel tightly and brake gently.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows, hold the wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by easing off the gas and using light braking. Pull off the road safely when possible.

questions.question: Because motorcycles and scooters are hard to see, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Look around constantly.
Share a lane with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look around constantly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles and scooters can hide in blind spots or be missed because they are small. Always watch carefully for them.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and be careful.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and wait until the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be careful.
questions.explanation: At a flashing yellow light, slow down and proceed carefully. You do not need to stop completely.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Stay farther back than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back than usual.
questions.explanation: Keep a 3 to 4 second distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly. If you follow too closely, you could hit the rider if they fall. This risk is higher on wet, icy, or gravel roads and on metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.

questions.question: What should you do to pass safely on a two-lane road?

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are traveling. Always make sure you can safely change lanes before passing. If you are unsure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait until it passes before you pass the car in front of you.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic?

options.text: Use your rearview and side mirrors.
Use your rearview mirror.
Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic when entering a freeway. This helps you spot vehicles you might miss with mirrors alone.

questions.question: What should you do if bad weather makes it hard to see?

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther back from the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: When you cannot see clearly due to darkness or bad weather, increase your distance from the car ahead. This gives you more time to react to dangers you cannot see.
